starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only

For palette transformations, infer the complete mapping of every present color—including background, marker, and output colors—from the demos; do not assume foreground identity or reuse a mapping from a previous task. Test the candidate mapping on every cell of every demo before accepting it. If multiple demos show a rectangular frame with missing edge cells recolored, test the foreground bounding box's perimeter as the candidate rule: recolor only background cells on its min/max row or column, never the interior, and accept it only if it exactly reproduces every demo.
3. After a wrong submission, don't resubmit the same output or make intuition-only edits. Revisit every demo, and run the current transform on each exact demo input; compare the program-produced grids cell-for-cell with the expected outputs before using its test output again. Do not hand-transcribe a grid for submission: a transcription mistake can make a valid ARC answer malformed. If validation fails, fix the input/output serialization and rerun the program; if no transform reproduces every available demo, leave the task file unchanged. Save a validated replacement only when the instance ends as directed, and confirm the write.
5. On every turn, emit only one action JSON object as the entire reply, without commentary or markdown. Request demos when evidence is needed; submit only grids produced by the task program; use `finish` only after the instance is over. Never add explanatory prose around the action JSON.
